-9467812.0235 5015679.9223000035.detail: PROJECT ANNOUNCEMENT MADE: An unnamed Fortune 100 company, operating under the code name 'Project Zodiac,' plans to build a 12-building data center campus on 500 acres of land in southeast Fort Wayne. Mayor Tom Henry announced the project at a press conference, describing it as a transformative investment for the region. The company's identity was not disclosed at the time.

ALLEN COUNTY PLAN COMMISSION UNANIMOUSLY APPROVES ANNEXATION RECOMMENDATION: The Allen County Plan Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval of the land annexation for Project Zodiac. 
Pushback: Residents expressed frustration during the meeting about the lack of transparency regarding the project's identity.

FORT WAYNE PLAN COMMISSION UNANIMOUSLY RECOMMENDS REZONING: The Fort Wayne Plan Commission voted unanimously to recommend approval of the rezoning of the Project Zodiac site from agricultural to industrial use. The recommendation was forwarded to the Fort Wayne City Council for final approval.

ANNEXATION APPROVED BY COUNTY COMMISSIONERS: Allen County Commissioners have cast their vote on the annexation of land for a new data center. Commissioners voted 3-0 to approve the annexation, which leaders say is the final vote in the matter. The land annexation is part of "Project Zodiac" a data center project. Rezoning was already approved: https://www.wane.com/top-stories/its-a-great-project-county-commissioners-sign-off-on-rezoning-for-data-center-campus/

AIR PERMIT APPLICATION SUBMITTED

REDEVELOPMENT COMMISSION APPROVES LAND SALE FOR PROJECT ZODIAC: The Fort Wayne Redevelopment Commission voted to approve the sale of city-owned land at 5801 Adams Center Road to Hatchworks LLC (Google's subsidiary) for the data center campus. The sale price was 4.6 million on 01/10/2024

INITIAL AIR OPERATING PERMIT APPROVED — 36 GENERATORS (PERMIT NO. 48739-00530): IDEM approved Hatchworks LLC's Title V Operating Permit for 36
-9467812.0235 5015679.9223000035.actionedBy: Indiana Dept. of Environmental Management (IDEM); Public

-9467812.0235 5015679.9223000035.detail: FIRST POWER — SITE ENERGIZED BY I&M: Indiana Michigan Power (I&M/AEP) energized the Google Fort Wayne data center site in November 2024, delivering first power to the campus approximately six months after the April 2024 groundbreaking. This milestone was confirmed in sworn regulatory testimony filed by I&M with the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (IURC) on July 30, 2025 (Cause No. 46276).

IURC APPROVES LARGE LOAD TARIFF SETTLEMENT (CAUSE NO. 46097): The Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission approved Indiana Michigan Power's Large Load Service Tariff settlement, establishing a new rate structure for hyperscale data center customers including Google's Fort Wayne facility. The tariff was the first of its kind in Indiana and set a precedent for how utilities can charge large industrial customers for dedicated infrastructure.
-9467812.0235 5015679.9223000035.actionedBy: Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission (IURC); Indiana Michigan Power (I&M/AEP)

-9467812.0235 5015679.9223000035.detail: GOOGLE–I&M DEMAND RESPONSE & CLEAN CAPACITY AGREEMENT FILED WITH IURC: Google and Indiana Michigan Power filed a joint contract with the IURC under which Google will voluntarily reduce its data center electricity consumption during grid stress events in exchange for clean energy capacity credits. The agreement was described as the first of its kind between a utility and a hyperscale data center operator in the US.

AIR PERMIT MODIFICATION APPLICATION FILED — 179 GENERATORS (PERMIT NOS. 48739 & 48840): Hatchworks LLC filed an application with IDEM to significantly modify its existing air operating permit to increase the number of emergency diesel generators from 36 to 179 (an increase of 143 units) and add 179 diesel fuel storage tanks. If approved, the 179 generators could collectively generate up to 527.52 MW and emit over 980 tons per year of regulated air pollutants.
ENVIRONMENTAL REGULATORY REVIEW  of Data Center: Indiana Department of Environmental Management (IDEM) granted Google permission to fill more than two acres of wetlands with soil

AEP WETLAND FILL PERMIT APPLICATION FOR TRANSMISSION LINE: American Electric Power (AEP) filed an application with IDEM to temporarily fill 0.13 acres of wetlands for the construction of a new high-voltage transmission line to supply power to the Google Fort Wayne data center.
-9467812.0235 5015679.9223000035.actionedBy: American Electric Power (AEP); Indiana Dept. of Environmental Management (IDEM)

-9467812.0235 5015679.9223000035.detail: AEP TRANSMISSION LINE WETLAND PERMIT APPROVED: IDEM approved AEP's application to temporarily fill wetlands for the construction of the transmission line serving the Google data center campus. The approval cleared the way for AEP to complete the high-voltage infrastructure needed for Phase 2 power delivery.

CITY COUNCIL HOLDS DRAINAGE CONTRACT — DEMANDS GOOGLE PAY: The Fort Wayne City Council voted unanimously at its December 9, 2025 meeting to hold approval of a $197,986 drainage culvert contract, demanding that Google pay for the work rather than Fort Wayne taxpayers. Council members argued that the drainage work was necessitated by Google's construction activity.
DATA CENTER OPERATIONAL: Google's $2 billion data center project in Fort Wayne, Indiana, commenced operations, supporting services such as Google Maps and Gemini AI, and Google Cloud services.

GOOGLE AGREES TO PAY $197,986 IN DRAINAGE COSTS — COUNCIL APPROVES CONTRACT: Following the December 9, 2025 hold, the Fort Wayne City Council approved the drainage culvert contract after Google agreed to reimburse the city for the full $197,986 cost.

-9409144.6368 3955367.3567999974.detail: [STATEWIDE — APPLIES TO COVINGTON] PSC APPROVES NEW RULE FOR DATA CENTER POWER USAGE: The Georgia PSC unanimously approved a new rule establishing minimum billing requirements for large-load customers (>100 MW) like data centers. Data centers must pay upfront the full local costs of serving them, commit to 5-15 year contracts, and provide financial guarantees. Any contract with >100 MW customer must be submitted to PSC for review at least 30 days before execution.
